page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, which rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Its memory subsystem also achieves top-tier results in small-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory tests. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, indicating that the server's strength lies primarily in parallelized, multi-threaded execution.

The server is optimized for highly parallel workloads such as software compilation, database operations, and static web serving, where it achieves top-tier throughput. It is also suitable for multi-threaded decompression tasks. However, it exhibits average performance for large-model LLM inference and cryptographic operations, and the lack of local NVMe storage means storage-heavy database workloads must rely entirely on network-attached storage. The ARMv9 architecture offers qualitative cost efficiency by delivering high multi-core compute density and memory bandwidth per resource unit without the overhead of hyperthreading.
